html:
The Ocloya were an Indigenous people of the forested valleys of eastern Jujuy in northwestern Argentina, between the high Quebrada de Humahuaca and the lowlands.

They were neighbours and often allies of the Omaguaca and lived near the Chichas. They held out against Spanish rule into the 1600s, and Spanish settlers then moved survivors onto estates. Little is known of their language. The town site of Tastil lies to the south.
sum: The Ocloya were an Indigenous people of the forested valleys of eastern Jujuy in northwestern Argentina, between the high Quebrada de Humahuaca and the lowlands.
